messages:
Jane (support): FYI customer 'AcmePayments' opened an escalation — large spike ~10:30 UTC, many /v1/generate calls returning 502/504, timeouts in client, saw errors ~10-60s. They reported latency >5s then upstream 5xx. They think this coincides with a traffic burst from a batch job.:alarm_clock:
Derek (oncall-sre): tagged. Can we get the correlation with k8s events and HPA/KEDA logs? Suspect scale-up lag. Any recent changes to KEDA config?
ops-bot: k8s event: 2026-02-28T10:31:02Z Pod inference-xyz terminated - OOMKilled
ops-bot: HPA event: 2026-02-28T10:31:10Z HPA inference-hpa scaled from 2 to 5 (target avg CPU 60%)
ops-bot: KEDA scaler: Trigger 'queue-length' fired, scale to 20 requested, last poll 10:31:12Z
Maria (runtime): Noted. Runtime logs show model load time ~9s for a cold-started container (quantized model) and readiness probe delay 8s. That adds up with the KEDA scale request -> but actual pods became Ready at ~10:39. That's ~8 minutes lag.
Kevin (prod): customer timeline: spike at 10:30, errors start 10:31, client retries amplify. By 10:40 errors reduced once we manually scaled.
Derek (oncall-sre): 8-minute provisioning sounds like pod warmup + scheduling + image pull? Check events for ImagePullBackOff or node shortage. Also check KEDA cooldown or polling interval - if it's too long it can underreact.
ops-bot: Node autoscaler events: cluster-autoscaler triggered 10:32:00Z -> new node ready 10:37:40Z
Jane (support): Customer wants a mitigation/what happened and repro steps. They're worried about SLAs.
Derek (oncall-sre): Immediate mitigations we applied: 1) kubectl scale deploy inference --replicas=10 (manual) 2) patched HPA minReplicas=5 to avoid full cold start on next spike 3) lowered KEDA cooldown from 300s to 60s. Notified customer.
Maria (runtime): Root cause summary guess: chain of events: sudden burst -> existing pods saturated -> KEDA detected queue but requested large scale -> cluster-autoscaler needed to add nodes -> nodes came up only after ~5m -> new pods then had model cold-start (~9s) + readiness probe -> total latency before capacity ~6-8 minutes. Meanwhile gateway timed out requests -> 502/504, upstream connection resets.
Derek (oncall-sre): Repro steps for us to validate locally (put in runbook):
1) Use a synthetic client to spike concurrent requests to hosted endpoint: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d @payload.json -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' with 300 concurrency for 60s.
2) Ensure cluster autoscaler has 0 spare nodes and HPA/KEDA minReplicas low so scale-up is required.
3) Observe KEDA poll logs: kubectl logs -n keda deploy/keda-operator -c keda || kubectl get scaledobjects
4) Watch events: kubectl get events -n inference --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp
5) Measure time from first KEDA trigger to first pod Ready and from first pod Ready to first successful request.
Maria (runtime): Add the following PromQL checks to the runbook: 
- increase_time_to_ready = time() - kube_pod_start_time_seconds{job=\"kubelet\", label_app=\"inference\"}
- queue_len = sum(app_queue_length) by (service)
- node_provisioning = predict_linear(kube_node_status_condition{condition=\"Ready\"}[10m])
Derek (oncall-sre): Commands we used in incident: 
- kubectl describe hpa inference-hpa -n inference
- kubectl get scaledobject -n inference -o yaml
- kubectl get pods -l app=inference -o wide --show-labels -n inference
- kubectl logs deploy/inference -c runtime --since=20m | grep \"model load\"
Maria (runtime): Found a config mismatch: KEDA scaledObject was pointing at a custom metric 'rabbitmq_queue_messages_ready' with a target of 1000 but our queue metric was reporting in a different unit (per-shard). So KEDA under-requested until multiple triggers aggregated. Also the KEDA pollingInterval was 30s and cooldownPeriod 300s — that explains slow reaction.
Kevin (prod): Also saw HPA CPU target set to 60% but the runtime is IO-bound; CPU is a poor signal. HPA wasn't effective at driving pods in time.
Derek (oncall-sre): Short-term actions (done): 
- manual scale to 12 replicas (still in place)
- increase HPA.minReplicas to 6
- reduce KEDA cooldown to 60s, pollingInterval to 10s for this scaledObject
- created hot-warm pool: set deployment annotation 'redwood/warmup=true' and an emergency sidecar that preloads model weights on start (testing).
Longer-term actions (todo): 
- add a pre-warm fleet for critical models (min idle replicas across cluster)
- move KEDA to use a more accurate aggregated metric (queue length across shards)
- use custom readinessProbe that becomes Ready only after runtime accepts first warmup RPC, not just process start
- update runbook to include node provisioning delay expectations and add a playbook to pre-scale nodes when expected spikes hit threshold
Maria (runtime): Patch proposal for runtime: add a lightweight background model cache layer so cold-start goes under 2s for common smaller models, and expose model_load_seconds metric with histogram.
Jane (support): Customer-facing blurb drafted: \"We identified a scale-up delay caused by cluster node provisioning and cold-start model loading. We've applied temporary configuration changes (raised minimum replicas and decreased scaler cooldowns) and are implementing pre-warm and metric fixes to avoid recurrence. Will follow up with timeline and RCA.\" They asked for ETA on permanent fixes.
Derek (oncall-sre): ETA: hot-warm pool 2 weeks to prototype, runtime cache 3-4 weeks, KEDA metric fix 1 week. Will confirm timeline with eng leadership.
ops-bot: note: Incident recorded ID INC-20260228-0421
Kevin (prod): Follow-ups: please ensure billing doesn't auto-charge customer for manual mitigation replicas — mark as goodwill credit if needed. Also check if request retries from client caused rate-limited backend throttling — re-evaluate client retry policy.
Maria (runtime): For reproducibility, here's a minimal script to run locally against dev cluster: 
```
# spike.sh
for i in $(seq 1 400); do
  curl -s -X POST https://dev.api.redwood/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEV_KEY" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' &
done
wait
```
Use kubectl top, keda-operator logs, and `kubectl get pods --watch` to time readiness.
Derek (oncall-sre): I'll own updating runbook + postmortem. Assigning action items: Maria -> runtime cache proposal and model_load metric. Kevin -> customer billing credit and comms. Jane -> customer follow-up message + timeline. Ops -> change KEDA polling/cooldown config and monitor for 24h.
Jane (support): Acknowledged. Sending current mitigation summary to customer now.
Derek (oncall-sre): Closing loop: we should add an SLO for scale-up time (trigger->ready) and alert if > 120s for critical models. Adding to backlog and will propose PR.
Maria (runtime): Also flag: readinessProbe currently uses TCP port only; change to a small /health/warmup endpoint that returns 200 only after model init. Will PR tonight.
ops-bot: Reminder: scheduled maintenance window at 2026-03-01T02:00Z - unrelated.
Jane (support): Thanks everyone — keeping thread open until RCA doc is published.
